title: Focus Architecture — Daily Hypothesis Sheet
body:
Purpose: lightweight daily/weekly scratchpad to treat focus as an engineering problem. Use as a quick hypothesis tracker for attention experiments and a compact KPI snapshot for the week. This is intentionally sparse — act as a single-pane-of-glass for the week so I don't open five different trackers.

How I think about this (micro-framework):
- North-star: "meaningful-merge-rate" = merged-feature-PRs / week that required >2 days deep work.
- Signal layer: fast, noisy, interpretable metrics only (no vanity metrics). Keep at most 3 signals per week.
- Control layer: anchors (timeboxes), noise budget (interruptions cap), and an experiment schedule (max 2 simultaneous experiments).

This doc = daily row + weekly rollup + retrospective notes.

---------
Daily hypothesis template (one line each morning):
- Hypothesis: what I expect will change if I adopt X (timebox, blocker removal, no-meeting chunk)
- Test: concrete action  — e.g., 90min deep-block at 9:30, phone on DND, no Slack pings
- Metric: which signal I will look at tonight (e.g., "focused-hours", "context-switches")
- Confidence: 1–5
- Quick note (end of day): outcome + 1 sentence learning

Example day (2026-03-09):
- Hypothesis: Shifting deep-work to 9:30 reduces context switches and increases flow — will finish the core API integration.
- Test: 90min closed-block, limited Slack, I will batch async reviews to afternoon.
- Metric: focused-hours = 1.5, switches = 2, PR progression: feature branch -> first review
- Confidence: 3
- End note: achieved focused window, PR pushed to review; still had one urgent meeting that fragmented afternoon. Learn: schedule an "urgent triage" block at 4p on heavy days.

---------
Weekly rollup (compact) — use at weekly check-in, 10–15 min.
Columns: week-start | north-star (meaningful merges) | focused-hours | avg switches/hr | top experiment | outcome | next-3-actions

2026-02-24 | 1 merge (feature) | 7.2h | 0.9 | morning-blocks | partial win (merge drafted) | 1) lock 9:30 block, 2) pause notifications, 3) schedule review times
2026-03-02 | 0 merges | 5.1h | 1.6 | meeting-surgery | fail (too many meetings) | 1) propose meeting-free mornings, 2) shorter agendas, 3) delegate quick syncs
2026-03-09 | 1 merge | 8.0h | 1.1 | inbox-sprint | win (core merged) | 1) standardize PR template, 2) pair-review on complex diffs, 3) capture blockers earlier

Signal definitions (so numbers are stable):
- focused-hours: contiguous time blocks >=45m spent on single project (sum per day)
- switches/hr: count of task context changes (calendar + manual notes) divided by active hours
- meaningful-merge: feature/change that: required design/architecture work and had >1 review round

---------
Experiment log (active / concluded):
- morning-blocks (active, started 2026-02-21): expected +1 focused hour/day. Observed +0.8h on average. Notes: high variance when PM schedules meetings after 9AM. Action: reserve hard calendar slot and add "no school" blocker to team.
- meeting-surgery (concluded, 2026-03-05): targeted to reduce ad-hoc syncs. Observed: cancellations reduced but backlog of async decisions grew. Decision: allow 1 meeting per week that can be expanded to async doc.

---------
Mini retro (questions to answer; quick bullets):
- What helped focus this week?
  - Blocked Slack in morning, paired with Ari for 45m
  - Clear checklist on PR descriptive template
- What got in the way?
  - Two urgent cross-team meetings, unclear owners
  - Surprise production bug on Thu that ate 3h
- Most surprising learning:
  - Small daily rituals (quick morning commit message checklist) reduced later rework by reducing ambiguity.
- One habit to drop:
  - Scanning inbox continuously in the morning. Replace with a 30-min inbox sprint after lunch.

Action items (measurable, owner, due):
- Create PR template with checklist (owner: me, due: 2026-03-12)
- Propose "Meeting-free mornings" doc to manager (owner: me, due: 2026-03-15)
- Add "urgent triage" 30m slot at 4p local on heavy days (owner: me, due: next week)

---------
Risks / open questions (notes to self):
- Team culture might resist meeting-free mornings; need a compact rationale (synchronous cost vs async ROI)
- How to measure true impact of focus on product velocity versus luck of task complexity? Consider pairing with product lead for a joint cadence metric.

---------
Reference snippets / copy-paste zone (use during write-ups):
- "Signal-first approach: three reliable signals, one north-star. Treat focus as telemetry."
- "Noise budget: cap interruptions to X/day and measure burn rate." 

---------
Quick checklist before Friday retro:
- export week rows into weekly email to manager (include numbers)
- surface two wins + one blocker in 3 bullet lines
- attach PR links and short context

Linked items I often paste:
- PR: github.com/org/repo/pull/481 — feature: compact-caching
- Retro note: confluence.redwood/workspaces/focus-principles (draft)
- Slack thread: #focus-architecture (pinned conversation)

---------
Notes to self (raw):
- If I feel momentum, double down on morning blocks for 3 consecutive days then measure. Momentum compound effect is real.
- When delegating, always add the "done/blocked" expected signal to avoid surprises.

---------
End state I want in 12 weeks:
- weekly meaningful-merge rate >= 2 consistently
- focused-hours average >= 9h/week with switches/hr < 0.8
- team adopted at least one meeting-surgery policy (e.g., async-updates + one weekly touch)

---------
Status: draft. Keep this lean; copy to a fresh "week-archive" doc at month end.
